items.title: Iran's war within a war may be about to begin
items.description: On Iraq's border with Iran troops are amassing as Iranian Kurds from across the globe gather to revolt after 47 years of being the victims of an oppressive and cruel regime.

items.title: There's one risky way to bypass Iran's oil blockade. Plus what else you should know today
items.description: The ABC's global affairs editor, Laura Tingle, is in Dubai and will provide daily updates on the Middle East war.

items.title: Live: Netanyahu makes veiled threat against Iran's new supreme leader
items.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu holds his first press conference since the war began and gives a veiled threat to kill Iran's new supreme leader. Follow live.

items.title: Live: Non-essential Australian officials directed to leave UAE, Israel
items.description: Non-essential Australian officials in the United Arab Emirates and Israel have been directed to leave as the security situation in the region deteriorates. Follow live.

items.title: Live: Oil hits $US100 again as Middle East supply shocks continue
items.description: Wall Street has traded sharply lower overnight as pessimism about the length of the war in the Middle East continues. Follow the day's events and insights as they happen with our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Trump's war tests his 'maybe less enthusiastic' VP Vance
items.description: From MAGA-loathing "hillbilly" to vice-president, JD Vance's rise and rebirth have been something to behold. But the war in Iran may test his considerable political dexterity.

items.title: 'Didn't even have their passports': Activists fear for Iranian footballers
items.description: Iranian activists are racing against time to convince members of the country's female football team to turn back from Malaysia, as fears grow that the women are being coerced home by regime officials.

items.title: Crocodiles found 'galloping' over roads, lurking near homes amid NT floods
items.description: Crocodiles have been spotted lurking in floodwaters across the Top End, with NT Police incident controller Shaun Gill warning the reptiles are "absolutely everywhere" right now.

items.title: Richardson's exit reinforces questions about royal commission
items.description: As soon as the royal commission was announced, Dennis Richardson must have known his situation was going to be tricky.

items.title: MP whose electorate gets largest capital gains tax discount wants to rein it in
items.description: New analysis shows five of the six electorates with the largest capital gains tax discount benefits are held by independents.

items.title: Estonia urges allies to brace for Russian veterans after Ukraine war
items.description: Estonia's foreign minister declares that Europe was like an "old, fat, lazy cat" in the aftermath of the Cold War and has vowed that NATO forces will strike "into the heart of Russia" if Moscow invades Baltic countries.

items.title: Is it possible to take money out of politics?
items.description: Through political donations, moneyed interests are able to access the political process in a way the average Australian simply can not. In an attempt to take money out of politics, South Australian Premier Peter Malinauskas has banned most political donations in the state and capped campaign spending by third parties. Party campaigning is now publicly funded, but the funding is tied to how many votes a party gets, which critics say makes it hard for minor parties or new independents. Now a state election will test if it makes politics fairer.

items.title: When the Matildas played in North Korea a full stadium laughed at them
items.description: When the Matildas played North Korea in Pyongyang in 2007, it was like unlike anything they had experienced before.

items.title: The one reason Latrell Mitchell broke his long-held media silence
items.description: NRL superstar Latrell Mitchell opens up about the Winmarra foundation, which he co-founded to empower emerging Indigenous leaders.

items.title: For a renowned actor, Hugo Weaving lives a very un-Hollywood life
items.description: Hugo Weaving may be an internationally renowned actor of both stage and screen, but he says he never feels ready for his next big role.

items.title: What Pokémon has to do with rare Australian insects
items.description: As Pokémon turns 30, a video game inspired by insect-collecting continues to shape how scientists think and teach about bugs today.

items.title: Weekly news quiz: A new Nationals leader and a curious crocodile
items.description: Think you've been paying attention to the news cycle this week? Test your memory here.

items.title: Outback Queensland town prepares for flooding as Bundaberg clean-up begins
items.description: Hundreds of people in Queensland's Bundaberg region are cleaning up their homes and businesses as floodwaters recede, while residents in western Queensland prepare for flooding.

items.title: 'Absolute disaster': Flood damage in SA raises concerns about road funding
items.description: As floodwater recedes and local governments begin calculating the damage to SA roads, they are frustrated it will be up to them to foot the bill in lieu of federal government support.

items.title: What should you do with the family home after a divorce?
items.description: For many Australians, the decision to divorce has become even more complicated because of the rising cost of housing. Some are now calling for policy changes to make it easier for single parents to re-enter the housing market.

items.title: SA Premier apologises for failing to deliver on his promise to 'fix the ramping crisis'
items.description: South Australian Premier Peter Malinauskas says there is "no shirking the fact" his government has failed to deliver on its key election promise to fix the ramping crisis — a failure for which he has apologised.

items.title: Swim rescue hero Austin Appelbee honoured by Irish president
items.description: Perth schoolboy Austin Appelbee, who heroically swam for hours to save the lives of his mum and two siblings off the WA coast, is honoured with a note from Ireland's President Catherine Connolly.

items.title: Oil tankers burn as Iran's new leader vows to keep Strait of Hormuz closed
items.description: Iran's new supreme leader says the Strait of Hormuz should remain closed as a tool of pressure, vowing to "obtain compensation from the enemy".

items.title: Trump says Iran welcome to play World Cup, but risk 'life and safety'
items.description: US President Donald Trump says Iran men's national soccer team is welcome to participate in the 2026 World Cup, but believes it is not appropriate that they be there "for their own life and safety".

items.title: 'Absolute madness': Broncos remain winless after Eels win bizarre NRL clash
items.description: The Broncos' defence is labelled "pathetic" as they surrender a 20-6 lead, hit back in the second half but eventually lose 40-32 on the back of future teammate Jonah Pezet's game-sealing try.
